# Dispatched audits: use both cheap slots during Phase 2 deep analysis

## Problem statement

The downtime worker pins `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1` for dispatched audits (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS) so an audit's Phase 2 child deep-analysis runs strictly sequentially (parent first, then one child at a time). This guarantees one audit fits cheap mode's 2-slots (parent + 1 child = 2) — but it also means a single dispatched audit NEVER uses more than one slot at a time during almost its entire run: Phase 1 is a single stream, and Phase 2 children serialize.

Proxy usage analysis of the 04:00-06:00 cheap window (2026-08-22) shows the local model busy only ~25-38% while these audits ran — the second slot sat idle. The audit chain ran 17 child sessions with ~12s gaps, then multi-minute gaps between dispatched runs.

Raising the fan-out to 2 would let one child run concurrently with the parent (2 slots busy) during deep analysis — but the current bound (WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS) exists precisely to keep child-heavy audits inside the cheap 2-slot pool. Parent + 2 children = 3 concurrent streams would fall back to remote. This item must therefore be coordinated with the concurrent-dispatch item so the combined in-flight stream budget never exceeds cheap capacity (2 slots).

## Users

- **Operator (rgardler)** — wants higher overnight local utilization without pushing more traffic to fallback (429-capped) remotes.
- **Herdr downtime users** — want child-heavy audits to complete faster.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Phase 2 deep-analysis concurrency for dispatched audits is mode-aware: 1 (current serial behavior) in fast mode or whenever the combined dispatch budget would exceed the cheap 2-slot pool; 2 when a second slot is genuinely free (coordinated with the concurrent-dispatch item).
2. Parent + N children as a single audit run never produces more concurrent local streams than the cheap-mode slot budget (2 in cheap mode).
3. No audit-skill changes (agent-infrastructure boundary — the skill already honours the env var); change lives in `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`).
4. Tests: env var value is mode/budget-dependent; spawn options for cheap mode with a free second slot include `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM: '2'`; fast mode or full pool keeps `'1'`.
5. Measured outcome: dispatched audit Phase 2 wall-clock drops (children overlap the parent) and/or cheap-window busy % rises vs. the 25-38% baseline, without increasing remote fallback rate.

## Notes

- History: WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (completed) set `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM=1` with rationale "cheap mode = 2 slots = parent + 1 child" — the audit skill default is 2, which the bound overrode to prevent 3-stream fallback. This item revisits that bound for the slot-idle case rather than reverting it.
- Default `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` handling lives in `audit_runner.py` (`AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM_ENV` / legacy alias) — pinned env in the pane spawn wins over the skill default.
- Related: WL-0MSG7P9N8009PCKG (same-slot idle tracking), WL-0MSORQ1RG005DGUS (fan-out bound), plus the proxy usage report's recommendation #3.
data.title: Dispatched audits: use both cheap slots during Phase 2 deep analysis (mode-aware PARALLELISM)

# CLI safety: export/import help text warnings

## Context
After a destructive `wl import` incident in the SorraAgents project (a work item was moved between projects via export/import and the source DB was replaced), the operator requested (2026-08-27, Tableau-Card-Engine session herdr-1787866878):

> make the --help text for import and export much clearer. Warn that export will export the entire database and import will replace the entire database

## Change
- `src/commands/export.ts`: description now warns the export writes the entire database (all items, comments, dependency edges) to the JSONL file.
- `src/commands/import.ts`: description now warns import is destructive — it REPLACEs the entire database with only the items in the JSONL file.

Both are description-only changes to the CLI help; no behavior change.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `wl export --help` output contains the warning that export writes the entire database.
2. `wl import --help` output contains the warning that import is destructive and REPLACEs the entire database.
3. Existing test suite passes (the changes are description-only; no CLI behavior changes).
data.title: Warn in wl export/import --help that export dumps the whole DB and import REPLACEs it

# Herdr downtime dispatcher: allow blocked-status dispatch and remove the implement risk cap

## Goal

As an operator, I want the Herdr downtime dispatcher to select work items that are
`blocked` and work items whose risk exceeds the previous Medium ceiling, so that
critical work is not stranded behind lower-priority items and high-risk work can
be auto-dispatched.

## Problem statement

Two `critical` items were being skipped by the dispatcher while lower-priority
items were dispatched ahead of them:

1. `WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME` (critical, blocked, `intake_complete`) — the critical-first
   scan filtered on `status === 'open'`, so a `blocked` item was never selected;
   `classifyItemForDispatch` also returned `null` for any non-`open` status.
2. `WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9` (critical, open, `plan_complete`, risk `High`) — the
   implement risk cap (`if (risk > 2) return null;`) excluded it, and because its
   risk/effort were already populated the risk-effort tier did not re-evaluate it,
   leaving it undispatchable.

The operator has explicitly approved removing the risk cap **globally** (for all
priorities, not only critical) and treating `blocked` as an allowable dispatch
status.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** `classifyItemForDispatch` accepts `blocked` status for non-completed
  items (in addition to `open`), so a `blocked` item at the `idea`,
  `intake_complete`, or `plan_complete` stage is classified to its
  stage-appropriate dispatch kind (`intake` / `plan` / `implement`).
- **AC2:** `selectCriticalFirstCandidates` includes critical items whose status is
  `open` **or** `blocked` (the `needsProducerReview !== true` gate is retained).
- **AC3:** The pre-dispatch CAS claim uses the candidate's ACTUAL status as the
  `--if-status` guard, so a `blocked` candidate claims with `--if-status blocked`
  and is not aborted as `stale` / `claim-failed`.
- **AC4:** The implement risk cap in `classifyItemForDispatch` is removed —
  `risk > 2` no longer returns `null`; the effort cap (`effort > 3` → `null`) is
  retained.
- **AC5:** An `open`, `plan_complete` item with risk `High` (or `Critical`) and a
  within-cap effort classifies as `implement` (regression test added).
- **AC6:** Safety gates are preserved: the `needsProducerReview` exclusion, the
  code-freeze split-by-skill pause, the audit freshness/recency window, the
  active-audit single-flight check, and the review-queue depth hold are unchanged
  in behaviour.
- **AC7:** The full herdr test suite and the repository test suite pass.

## Out of scope / decisions

- The legacy, production-unreachable selection helpers (`selectImplementCandidate`,
  `selectCriticalCandidate`, `resolveDependencyFrontier`) are **not** on the live
  dispatch path (the Herdr-list head is the sole ranking source). Their risk cap
  is left unchanged to keep the change surgical; recorded here as a decision.
- No change to the effort cap.

## Discovered from

- `WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME` (critical, blocked) and `WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9` (critical,
  risk High) — the two critical items this change unsticks.
data.title: Herdr downtime dispatcher: allow blocked-status dispatch and remove the implement risk cap
